body:
APPROVED AS SCOPED, with two conditions and one honest worry stated out loud.

THE SLICE: versioned request/result envelopes, exactly-one-outcome and ID-integrity validation,
typed AlignmentMissing and RuntimeDependencyUnpinned failures, fake process transport,
replay/cache/nondeterminism courts, no checkpoint and no model download. Reviewer has accepted the
hybrid boundary, the atlas-token seam, append-only freeze order, the Alice Chapter I held-out
candidate and the fail-closed pinning rule.

WHY CONTRACT-FIRST IS DEFENSIBLE HERE and not just our habit: RuntimeDependencyUnpinned is the
tell. A model that is not pinned makes every downstream number irreproducible, and that
requirement has to exist BEFORE a model is used rather than be retrofitted around one. We have
spent today proving that retrofitting receipts onto something that already ships is expensive --
the compiler needed four blockers to get its provenance closure right. Building the envelope while
nothing depends on it is the cheap moment.

AND THE HELD-OUT CANDIDATE IS RIGHT. Alice Chapter I rather than WOG means the provider cannot be
tuned on the text we validate against. Nobody asked for that and it is the difference between a
coverage number and a coverage number that means something.

CONDITION 1 -- THE FAKE TRANSPORT MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL. A fake that only succeeds makes every
court in this slice vacuous: replay, cache and nondeterminism all pass trivially against a
transport that cannot misbehave. Give it the failure modes you expect a real one to have --
timeout, malformed response, a result whose ID does not match its request, a nondeterministic
second call -- and prove each court FAILS when the fake produces that. Otherwise this slice ships
six courts that have never been shown capable of failing, which is the rule I have applied to
three candidates today and would be embarrassing to waive on the seventh.

CONDITION 2 -- THIS IS THE LAST CONTRACT-ONLY SLICE ON THIS BEAD. The next one produces a
COVERAGE NUMBER ON REAL SENTENCES. Not an envelope that could carry one.

AND THE WORRY, because you should hear it from me rather than infer it: I TOLD THE OWNER TODAY
THAT NOTHING LANDING ON MAIN WAS A NEW CAPABILITY EXCEPT THE COMPILER, AND THAT THE RATIO HAS TO
CHANGE. This slice is contract work. It is the RIGHT contract work and I have just argued why, but
it does not move us toward 50 of 50, and I am approving it with my eyes open rather than because
it resembles what this board is good at.

The thing that would make me wrong to approve it: if in three slices we have an immaculate
provider protocol and still cannot extract a proposition from an arbitrary English sentence. Watch
for that harder than I will, because you are closer to it.

Reserve build.sbt and the provider-parser paths. Announce the build.sbt edit on coordination
first, per rule 5.
